title: TAP states at upper deviations of the free energy: existence, localization and marginal stability in Ising spin glasses
abstract: We study upper large deviations of the free energy of mixed $p$-spin Ising spin glasses through the generalized TAP free energy $F_{\mathrm{TAP}}$ of Chen, Panchenko and Subag. For every mixture with radius of convergence greater than one, $\max F_{\mathrm{TAP}}$ and $\log Z_N$ have the same large deviations at speed $N$; the proof combines their band theorem with Ramsey's theorem. For convex mixtures with $\sum_p 2^pβ_p^2<\infty$, upper deviations at level $f$ are carried by generalized TAP critical points, which exist at the free-energy rate without Boursier's strict Plefka condition. Outside an event of smaller exponential order, near-maximizers at level $f$ lie near the contact set of a constrained Parisi obstacle, follow the Auffinger-Chen field law, and have Hessian bulk near a reflected Pastur law whose edge is nonpositive and vanishes exactly at contacts where the obstacle is flat to second order. Where every contact is of this kind, a fixed stability margin costs rate.
summary: This work rigorously analyzes the large deviation behavior of the free energy in mixed p-spin Ising spin glasses. It proves that these deviations are controlled by generalized Thouless-Anderson-Palmer (TAP) critical points. The methodology provides deep insights into the mathematical structure of disordered systems, extending classical results with advanced large deviation theory.
main_problem: The paper investigates the upper large deviations of the free energy in mixed p-spin Ising spin glasses.
main_result: It establishes that the large deviations are governed by generalized TAP critical points, providing precise rate functions for the free energy.
method: The analysis combines advanced techniques from large deviation theory, relating the free energy to the Parisi functional structure and utilizing comparison methods.
model_or_system: The study focuses on mixed p-spin Ising spin glasses defined on the hypercube {-1, 1}^N, characterized by their Hamiltonian and associated covariance functions $\xi(t)$.
key_observables: Free energy ($N^{-1} \log Z_N$), generalized TAP free energy ($F_{\text{TAP}}$), and the rate function $\Sigma(f)$.
important_parameters: The deviation level $f$, the radius of convergence of the covariance $\xi(t)$, and the perturbation parameter $\gamma$.
main_assumptions: Key assumptions include the radius of convergence of the covariance exceeding one, and the validity of the fractional moment formula (FM).
paper_structure: The paper builds by first relating $\max F_{\text{TAP}}$ to $\log Z_N$ (Theorem 1), then characterizing the structure of the maximizers via generalized TAP critical points (Theorem 2), and finally detailing the local structure using the field law and Hessian bulk (Theorem 3).
why_interesting: While focused on classical statistical mechanics, the mathematical tools used—such as analyzing complex energy landscapes and critical points—are highly relevant to understanding the complexity of quantum many-body systems and optimization problems in quantum information.
